items.followUp: Describe the tissue level of organization and give one example.

rubric.why: Defines an organ by its composition and function.
rubric.description: An organ is made of different tissues working together to perform a specific function.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it contains different tissues and 1 mark for their coordinated function.

rubric.why: A suitable example supports the explanation.
rubric.description: Gives a correct example of an organ.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming any valid organ.

rubric.why: Shows how the example organ performs a function.
rubric.description: States a correct function of the chosen example.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly linking the example to its function.

modelAnswer: An organ is a structure made up of different types of tissues that work together to perform a specific function.
For example, the stomach contains several tissues that work together to digest food.

items.followUp: Define the species level and list the taxonomic ranks from kingdom to species.

rubric.why: Identifies hierarchy as an ordered system of classification.
rubric.description: Defines taxonomic hierarchy as the arrangement of organisms in ranked groups.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the idea of classification in ranks or groups.

rubric.why: The ordered ranks are the central content of the answer.
rubric.description: Lists the taxonomic ranks in correct order from the largest group to the smallest.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for the correctly ordered sequence; allow division instead of phylum for plants.

rubric.why: Identifies the lowest rank in the hierarchy.
rubric.description: States that species is the smallest or basic taxonomic rank.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly identifying species as the lowest/basic rank.

modelAnswer: Taxonomic hierarchy is the arrangement of organisms into groups called taxa, in a series of ranked levels.
The ranks from largest to smallest are kingdom, phylum (or division in plants), class, order, family, genus and species.
Species is the smallest and basic unit of classification.

items.followUp: Describe the light reactions of photosynthesis and state where they occur.

rubric.why: A definition identifies the reactants and products of photosynthesis.
rubric.description: Defines photosynthesis as the process in which green plants use light energy to make glucose from carbon dioxide and water, releasing oxygen.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the essential idea of making food using light; accept a correct word equation or balanced equation.

rubric.why: The location distinguishes the dark reactions from the light reactions.
rubric.description: States that dark reactions occur in the stroma of chloroplasts.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct location.

rubric.why: Explains why these reactions are called dark reactions and identifies their inputs.
rubric.description: Explains that they do not directly require light and use ATP and NADPH made in the light reactions to fix carbon dioxide.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the light independence and use of products of the light reactions.

rubric.why: Carbon fixation is a key step in the Calvin cycle.
rubric.description: Describes carbon dioxide fixation and its conversion through intermediate compounds such as PGA and PGAL.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct account of carbon fixation and intermediate formation.

rubric.why: The cycle produces carbohydrate and regenerates its carbon dioxide acceptor.
rubric.description: States that carbohydrate is formed and/or RuBP is regenerated to continue the cycle.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct end product or regeneration of RuBP.

modelAnswer: Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants use light energy to make glucose from carbon dioxide and water, releasing oxygen.
Dark reactions occur in the stroma of the chloroplast and do not directly require light.
They use ATP and NADPH produced during the light reactions to fix carbon dioxide.
Carbon dioxide combines with RuBP and is converted through intermediate compounds, including PGA and PGAL.
Some PGAL is used to form glucose, while the remaining material regenerates RuBP.

items.followUp: Describe the structure, functions and sources of proteins.

rubric.why: The chemical composition and building components describe lipid structure.
rubric.description: States that lipids contain carbon, hydrogen and oxygen and are commonly made from glycerol and fatty acids.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the main elements and/or glycerol-fatty acid composition.

rubric.why: A distinguishing property or composition feature adds to the structural description.
rubric.description: Gives a correct structural property, such as being insoluble in water or having less oxygen than carbohydrates.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one valid property.

rubric.why: Lipids have important energy, structural and protective roles.
rubric.description: Names a correct function of lipids.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one or more valid functions.

rubric.why: Examples show dietary sources of lipids.
rubric.description: Names suitable sources of lipids.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving at least two valid sources.

modelAnswer: Lipids are organic compounds containing carbon, hydrogen and oxygen; they contain less oxygen than carbohydrates.
Many lipids are formed from glycerol and fatty acids and are insoluble in water.
Lipids store energy, form part of cell membranes, and provide insulation and protection.
Sources include vegetable oils, butter, ghee, nuts, seeds, meat and milk.

items.followUp: Define organs and name two plant organs and two animal organs.

rubric.why: A tissue is identified by its cells and their shared role.
rubric.description: Defines a tissue as a group of similar cells performing a particular function.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the definition.

rubric.why: Correct examples demonstrate knowledge of plant tissues.
rubric.description: Names two plant tissues and two animal tissues.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming two plant tissues and two animal tissues; accept other correct tissue names.

modelAnswer: A tissue is a group of similar cells that work together to perform a particular function.
Plant tissues: xylem and phloem.
Animal tissues: epithelial and muscular tissues.

items.followUp: What is agriculture? Name one activity included in it besides growing crops.

rubric.why: Horticulture is the specialized cultivation referred to in the question.
rubric.description: Defines horticulture as the cultivation of fruits, vegetables, flowers or ornamental plants.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct description of horticulture.

rubric.why: The distinction is that horticulture is a specialized branch while agriculture is broader.
rubric.description: Distinguishes horticulture from agriculture by explaining that agriculture covers broader crop production and may include animal rearing.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a clear, correct comparison.

modelAnswer: Horticulture is the cultivation of fruits, vegetables, flowers and ornamental plants.
It is a specialized branch of agriculture, while agriculture is broader and includes growing crops and may include rearing animals.

items.followUp: State two observations about a disease that could help investigate how it spreads.

rubric.why: These are characteristic observed symptoms of malaria.
rubric.description: Records a characteristic symptom, such as recurring fever with chills.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct observed symptom.

rubric.why: The association with mosquito presence or mosquito breeding areas is an important observation about malaria.
rubric.description: Notes malaria's association with mosquitoes or with areas where mosquitoes breed, such as stagnant water.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a relevant observation linking malaria with mosquitoes or their breeding places.

modelAnswer: Malaria patients may suffer from recurring fever, often accompanied by chills.
Malaria is commonly observed in areas where mosquitoes are abundant, particularly near stagnant water.

items.followUp: What is a hypothesis in the biological method?

rubric.why: Recognition is the initial identification of a problem for investigation.
rubric.description: Explains that recognition of a biological problem means identifying or noticing a problem in the living world that needs investigation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying/noticing the problem and 1 mark for stating that it is a biological problem to be investigated.

modelAnswer: Recognition of a biological problem is the identification or noticing of a problem related to living organisms that needs investigation.
